decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to maintain its benchmark interest rate target range at 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent.

changes.quote: The unemployment rate has stabilized at a low level in recent months, and labor market conditions remain solid.
changes.explanation: The Fed noted that labor market conditions have stabilized rather than continuing to ease.
The Fed removed reference to progress made toward its target, highlighting that inflation remains elevated.

changes.quote: In support of its goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent.
changes.explanation: The Fed paused its rate cuts to keep policy rates unchanged at this meeting.

tone_quotes.quote: The unemployment rate has stabilized at a low level in recent months, and labor market conditions remain solid.
The Committee judges that the risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals are roughly in balance.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 21.76% APR costs about $90.67 a month in interest.
Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate; the 10-year was 4.55% and moved 0 bp on the day, so the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 7.04% would not change.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.1%, and employers added an average of 135k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.9% over the past year, while core PCE inflation was 2.9%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.4% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield moved +2 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.47%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.05% on the day.

card.whats_next: The Fed indicated it will carefully assess incoming economic data before making future rate adjustments. Policymakers remain open to adjusting stance if unexpected economic risks emerge.
